alice: Quick thread — profiler is showing weird p99 spikes on several text-gen routes over the last 2 hours. Quick breakdown looks like input-stage (tokenization + KV lookup/serialization) ~= 40% of p99 and generation ~= 60%, but p95 is generation-dominated. Posting numbers.

ben: Can you paste the raw numbers?

alice: p95=220ms p99=620ms median=45ms. p99 gen=380ms, input-stage=240ms. Sample workload: seq_len=1024, microbatch=16, model=x-16q.

carlos: Did KV cache miss rate spike? That would blow up input-stage time.

alice: Yes — KV miss rate went from ~7% baseline to ~27% on affected windows. Also saw kernel fallback events when prefill paths hit sequence shapes we hadn’t optimized.

diana: We changed kernel-selection heuristic for long-prefill recently to prefer fused-attn. Could that cause regressions during decode (kernel-switching overhead)? Any flamegraphs/traces?

alice: Quick perf dump below (trimmed):

```
# perf summary (route: /gen-fast)
batch_size: 16
seq_len: 1024
kv_miss: 27%
kernel_calls:
  fused_attn_prefill: 52%
  decode_matmul: 28%
  kv_serialization: 12%
tail_latency_histogram: p95:220 p99:620 p999:980
```

ben: We should sweep microbatch sizes (8 vs 16 vs 32) and measure p95/p99. Also compare warm vs cold KV cache.

emily: I ran a short microbatch sweep yesterday: microbatch=8 -> p95 increased ~10% but p99 dropped ~30%. microbatch=32 -> p95 improved but p99 got worse. Looks like classic head vs tail throughput tradeoff.

frank: Proposed mitigations: 1) adaptive microbatcher that reduces batch size under queue/backlog to protect tail, 2) bump kernel-switch threshold to avoid fallback during prefill for known shapes, 3) early KV warmup for hot prefixes (background populate).

carlos: We need better telemetry first: histograms tagged by actual batch_size + kv_miss_flag + kernel_variant. Then we can correlate tail spikes to kernel variant / miss events.

diana: I'll roll a canary patch: add span tags `kernel_variant` and `kv_miss` to traces + config flag `microbatch.adaptive=true` (default false). Deploy to 10% for /gen-fast.

deploy-bot: canary started on cluster-us-east-1 for routes [/gen-fast] with microbatch.adaptive=true (10% traffic).

alice: Also thinking about short-term fixes: precompute KV keys for common prefixes and avoid serializing full KV on prefill when prefix matches. Long-term we should build a cost model for kernel selection (estimate per-token latency + SLO penalty) instead of fixed heuristics.

ben: Agree. Immediate ask: diana, can you run a regression bisect on the kernel-selection change? Suspect commit 6f9b2c introduced the fallback behavior change.

diana: On it. Will post OOO if I find the exact offending diff.

alice: Thanks — we'll monitor canary metrics over the next 2 hours. If p99 improves >20% we promote. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

frank: One more note — add a quick A/B with `microbatch.static=8` vs `adaptive` to see which strategy looks more stable under bursty traffic.

emily: I'll schedule that as part of the canary plan and attach graphs (p50/p95/p99 by kernel_variant) once data arrives.

carlos: Cool. After canary results, follow-up action items: kernel cost-model design doc, KV prefix cache experiment, and adaptive microbatch rollout playbook.

alice: Great — thanks everyone.
